The simulation models spray combustion of liquid dodecane in hot air inside a 2D axisymmetric cylindrical chamber.
The chamber is 0.2 m long and 0.1 m in diameter, with the symmetry axis along the centerline.
Model the domain as a 2D axisymmetric wedge representing the chamber radius.
Set the working pressure to 101325 Pa.
Initialize the chamber with air at 800 K and 101325 Pa.
Use the k-epsilon turbulence model with standard wall functions.
Set the air co-flow inlet at the left boundary to a velocity of (10 0 0) m/s, temperature 800 K, pressure 101325 Pa, and mass fractions O2=0.233 and N2=0.767.
Set the inlet turbulence intensity to 5% and the turbulent length scale to 0.01 m.
Set the outlet at the right boundary to a fixed pressure of 101325 Pa.
Treat the chamber walls as adiabatic, no-slip walls.
Neglect radiation heat transfer.
Inject liquid dodecane using a cone injection model.
Place the injector on the centerline at the left inlet plane, with the spray cone axis aligned with the chamber centerline and pointing downstream.
Set the spray cone half-angle to 30 degrees.
Set the dodecane mass flow rate to 0.002 kg/s.
Set the dodecane injection temperature to 300 K.
Use a Rosin-Rammler droplet size distribution with a mean diameter of 50e-6 m.
Assume a Rosin-Rammler spread parameter of 3.5, a minimum droplet diameter of 1e-6 m, and a maximum droplet diameter of 100e-6 m.
Assume an injector nozzle diameter of 0.2 mm, giving an injection velocity of approximately 85 m/s derived from the mass flow rate and nozzle area.
Use finite-rate combustion with the two-step global n-dodecane mechanism.
Use the reaction C12H26 + 12.5 O2 -> 12 CO + 13 H2O.
Use the reaction CO + 0.5 O2 -> CO2.
Use Janaf thermodynamics for all species.
Set up the OpenFOAM case using the sprayFoam solver with constant/combustionProperties, constant/reactionSchemes, and janaf thermo tables accordingly.
